result.document_summary: California Civil Rights Department web page explaining state fair housing (FEHA) protections, including source-of-income and criminal-history limits on tenant screening.
result.notes: The page is mostly general fair housing guidance (discrimination, accommodations, modifications, harassment), which is out of scope. Two in-scope screening_restrictions rules were extracted under FEHA: source-of-income protection and criminal-history screening limits. The page gives no effective dates and names FEHA without a specific section number, so citation is the Act's name. No rent, eviction, deposit, fee, or algorithmic pricing rules appear.

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination prohibited (incl. Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on how a tenant pays rent, including Section 8 vouchers, SSI, rental assistance, or wages. They must also comply with rental assistance program paperwork and inspection requirements and may not advertise 'No Section 8'.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected characteristic
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.coverage_text: Applies to landlords, property managers, and other housing providers across most California rental housing.
rules.exemptions_text: Page notes limited exclusions for an owner-occupant renting to one additional person (discriminatory advertising still barred), shared living areas, and senior housing, though these are described mainly for other protected characteristics.

rules.title: Limits on criminal-history screening of rental applicants
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not use blanket bans. Denials based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and to not threaten the health and safety of others or the property.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; no non-conviction arrests, sealed/expunged or juvenile records
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to landlords, property managers, tenant screening companies, and other housing providers across most California rental housing.
